text.p: Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA/ Plc welcomed on Thursday news that P&O European Ferries and Stena Line AB of Sweden were merging their short sea ferry business on the English Channel.
"If, and only if, this agreement means a reduction in capacity, we welcome the news," a Eurotunnel spokeswoman said. "In that case, the sooner the better," she added.

Britain's P&O and Stena earlier announced they are putting 14 ships into a joint venture operating company in which P&O will hold 60 and Stena 40 percent. They aim to cut capacity and costs, following a savage price war with Eurotunnel.
That price competition gouged a hole in Eurotunnel's cashflow last year and helped pitch it into a unilateral decision to freeze interest on some 62 billion francs of junior bank debt last September.
Eurotunnel announced on Wednesday it had reached an agreement in principle with its bankers to restructure its debt and unpaid interest, now totalling around 70 billion francs.
